To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a novel, compact thermal model for nonlinear distributed thermal systems, which can be implemented within an electrothermal microwave circuit simulator.

we have developed a fully analytical, double-Fourier series, spectral domain decomposition method for the thermal modeling of complex 3-D nonlinear electronic systems, and that we have implemented it in a microwave circuit simulation program.
A new, fully analytical, compact, time-domain thermal modeling technique for nonlinear 3-d electronic systems is developed, based on a spectral domain decomposition approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a compact, fully physical, and fully analytical, thermal modeling approach for complex nonlinear, 3-d electronic systems.
developing a fully physical and accurate, compact, time-dependent electrothermal modeling methodology for power devices and circuits.

the development of an original, fully analytical spectral domain decomposition method for the time-dependent compact thermal modelling of complex, nonlinear, distributed thermal systems, and its integration within electrothermal CAD of power electronic devices and circuits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work has provided a new, fully analytical solution for the transient thermal modeling of complex electronic systems, which can be used for electrothermal CAD.
a fully analytical, time-domain, compact thermal model has been developed and validated, and implemented within a microwave CAD tool.
a fully physical, time-domain, thermal modeling solution has been achieved for the first time for arbitrary, complex, 3-D, distributed, nonlinear electronic systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a fully physical, analytical, time-dependent thermal modeling approach for complex nonlinear 3-D thermal systems, with minimal boundary conditions, and have demonstrated its implementation for fully coupled, time-domain, electrothermal, harmonic balance, circuit simulation.

the method presented is an original, fully analytical approach, based on double Fourier series expressions, to the time-dependent thermal analysis of complex nonlinear (three-dimensional) electronic systems.

we have demonstrated the feasibility of fully physical, time domain, compact thermal modeling for complex nonlinear electronic systems, and its compatibility with explicit coupled electrothermal device/circuit simulation, on CAD timescales, for the first time.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it provides the first time-dependent thermal modeling approach to complex, nonlinear, 3-D thermal systems, with a fully analytical, explicit, compact model, that is compatible with fully coupled, time-domain electrothermal device and microwave circuit CAD.
we have demonstrated a fully physical, time-domain, thermal modeling technique, which can be applied to complex 3-D nonlinear systems, and which can be directly incorporated into electrothermal CAD.
we have developed a novel, fully physical, time-dependent thermal modeling approach that is compatible with explicit, coupled electrothermal device/circuit simulation.
